title: Thermodynamic Structure and Composition in Nonlinear Convection-Diffusion
abstract: Nonlinear convection--diffusion systems play a central role in transport phenomena, including mass transfer, heat transfer, porous-media transport, and coupled continuum processes with source, exchange, and interface effects. In such systems, the key question is often not only which governing partial differential equation is used, but whether the model preserves a consistent thermodynamic balance under the operations that arise naturally in transport analysis: restriction to subdomains, coupling across interfaces, linearization near equilibrium, and discretization for computation.   This paper develops a continuum-first framework for open nonlinear convection--diffusion systems in which thermodynamic consistency is formulated as a free-energy balance with nonnegative bulk dissipation and explicit boundary and source contributions. Within this setting, nonlinear transport systems are defined as structured objects built from admissible state fields, storage functionals, constitutive flux decompositions, sources, and boundary ports. We prove that the thermodynamic balance is preserved under exact structure-preserving transformations, restriction to subdomains, local-to-global reconstruction over compatible domain decompositions, and power-conserving interconnection of open subsystems. We then derive classical linear convection--diffusion models as tangent thermodynamic descendants at equilibrium and show that the same invariant survives weak formulation, semidiscretization, and fully discrete time stepping when the numerical design respects thermodynamic structure. Nonlinear drift--diffusion and porous-medium convection--diffusion are used as explicit examples. The resulting contribution is a compositional transport framework in which the second law remains visible across continuum modeling, subsystem coupling, linear approximation, and computation.
summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive framework to ensure that nonlinear convection-diffusion models rigorously obey the second law of thermodynamics. It achieves this by defining thermodynamic consistency as an invariant property preserved across continuum modeling, subsystem coupling, linearization, and numerical discretization. The work provides a powerful structural tool for building physically consistent computational models in transport physics.
main_problem: Developing a rigorous mathematical framework for nonlinear convection-diffusion systems that guarantees the preservation of thermodynamic balance (the second law) across all modeling stages.
main_result: The authors prove that the free-energy balance is invariant under key operations like restriction to subdomains, interface coupling, and numerical discretization schemes.
method: The work employs a continuum-first framework built on defining open constitutive structures using free-energy functionals and analyzing structural preservation via categorical methods.
model_or_system: Open nonlinear convection-diffusion systems governing transport phenomena (mass/heat transfer) in fluids or porous media, modeled around a free-energy balance equation.

paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the continuous free-energy balance (Theorem 2.9), extends this to local/global reconstruction via category theory (Theorems 3.5, 4.5, 4.13), and finally applies these structural invariants to ensure consistency across semidiscrete and fully discrete numerical schemes (Theorems 7.4, 7.7).
why_interesting: While focused on classical transport, the rigorous mathematical machinery—especially the emphasis on structure preservation under approximation/decomposition—is highly relevant for developing consistent quantum field theories or open quantum system dynamics where approximations are unavoidable.
